skill.name: pr-prepare
skill.description: Reviews Git branch changes and prepares a structured pull request title and description using a consistent project template.
skill.summary: Turn current branch changes into a clear, review-ready pull request description.
skill.author: ByronWilliamsCPA

content.value_statement: Writing complete pull request descriptions from branch changes takes time and often misses important context. This skill reviews Git changes and produces a structured title and description.
actual_capabilities: Inspects Git status, branch commits, changed-file statistics, and the branch diff against the selected base.
Identifies modified components, purpose, impact, risks, breaking changes, and testing context.
Creates sections for summary, changes, impact, testing, and optional notes.
Suggests a pull request title using common conventional commit prefixes.
Presents a complete description and optional commands for pushing the branch and opening the pull request.
limitations: Assumes main as the base branch unless the user specifies another branch.
Uses its built-in format and does not discover a repository pull request template.
Does not run or verify tests and linting, so checklist status requires confirmation.
Does not automatically push changes or create the pull request.

use_cases.title: Describe a feature branch
use_cases.description: Convert a completed feature branch into a structured title and reviewer-focused pull request description.

use_cases.title: Standardize team submissions
use_cases.description: Apply consistent summary, impact, testing, and notes sections across pull requests.

use_cases.title: Prepare maintenance changes
use_cases.description: Summarize dependency, refactoring, performance, or documentation updates before repository review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare my current branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pull request title and description for my current branch against main. Keep test items unchecked unless verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a complete first draft.

prompt_templates.title: Use another base branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this branch against develop. Group changes by component and identify any breaking behavior or required follow-up work.
prompt_templates.scenario: A repository uses a development branch instead of main.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on a bug fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a bug-fix pull request. Explain the cause, changed behavior, affected components, regression coverage, and remaining risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs reviewers to understand a defect and its resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Build a release-ready description
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the branch and prepare a release-ready pull request. Separate verified tests from pending checks, and flag migrations, security effects, and compatibility risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs detailed review and release context.

output_examples.input: Prepare a pull request for a branch that adds OAuth login and authentication tests.
output: Suggested title: feat: add OAuth login
Summary: Adds provider login, callback handling, and secure session management.
Testing: Authentication tests were added, but execution status requires confirmation.

output_examples.input: Write a pull request description for a fix that prevents duplicate order processing.
output: Suggested title: fix: prevent duplicate order processing
Impact: Repeated delivery events no longer create duplicate orders.
Notes: Confirm retry behavior and database constraints before merge.

output_examples.input: Prepare a maintenance pull request for dependency updates and documentation changes.
output: Suggested title: chore: update dependencies and documentation
Changes: Updates project dependencies and aligns setup documentation with the current workflow.
Testing: Dependency compatibility and installation steps need verification.

best_practices: Confirm the correct base branch before generating the comparison.
State which tests and checks actually ran, and leave unverified items unchecked.
Review the generated description for sensitive data, inaccurate claims, and missing reviewer context.
anti_patterns: Do not mark tests as passed without execution evidence.
Do not use vague summaries that repeat the pull request title.
Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or unrelated secrets from the diff.

faq.question: Does this skill create the pull request?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the title and description, then provides optional commands for the user.

faq.question: Which base branch does it use?
faq.answer: It uses main by default. Specify another base branch when your repository uses a different workflow.

faq.question: Does it run tests or linting?
faq.answer: No. It includes checklist items, but the user must run and confirm each check.

faq.question: Can it follow my repository template?
faq.answer: It uses a built-in template. Provide repository-specific sections or requirements in the request.

faq.question: How does it choose a pull request title?
faq.answer: It maps the change purpose to a conventional prefix such as feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, perf, or chore.

faq.question: Can it handle large branches?
faq.answer: It can summarize them, but large diffs may require focused prompts or separate descriptions by component.
